### Overview:
For this homework assignment, I am going to:

* Load in my required libraries  
* Load and look at my data  
* Create a figure visualizing my data  
* Generate a table summarizing my data  
* Summarize general findings  

### 1. Loading libraries:

```{r}
#| message: false

library(palmerpenguins) #loading palmer penguins package with 'penguins' dataset
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
library(patchwork)
```

### 2. Loading data:

Dataset is already included in **palmerpenguins** package; has data on penguins from the Palmer Archipelago.

The dataset contains measurements for the variables: *`r head(names(penguins), -1)`*, and *`r tail(names(penguins), 1)`*.

```{r}
head(penguins) #looking at head of penguins data to remind myself of available variables
```

This dataset has data collected across **`r nrow(penguins)` total penguins**, with **`r n_distinct(penguins$species)` species** across **`r n_distinct(penguins$island)` islands**.

##### The `r n_distinct(penguins$species)` species included are:

![](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/reference/figures/lter_penguins.png)

##### Data was collected at the **Palmer Station LTER**, on the Antarctic Peninsula

![](https://education.rstudio.com/blog/2020/07/palmerpenguins-cran/antarctica-map.png)

### 3. Data analysis:
First, I'm generating density plots to visualize the spread of the body measurements collected across each of the `r n_distinct(penguins$species)` species in this dataset.
```{r}
#| label: fig-penguinplot #now this plot is labeled as "penguinplot" and can be called
#| fig-cap: "Density plots of bill depth, bill length, flipper length, and body mass for each of 3 species from Palmer LTER data. Count density (reflecting group size) is plotted for each measurement."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10
depth <- penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x=bill_depth_mm, fill=species))+
  geom_density(
    aes(y = after_stat(count)),
    alpha = 0.5,
    color = NA) + #getting rid of black outlines
  labs(
    x = "Bill Depth (mm)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Species") +
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

length <- penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x=bill_length_mm, fill=species))+
  geom_density(
    aes(y = after_stat(count)),
    alpha = 0.5,
    color = NA) + #getting rid of black outlines
  labs(
    x = "Bill Length (mm)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Species") +
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

flipper <- penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x=flipper_length_mm, fill=species))+
  geom_density(
    aes(y = after_stat(count)),
    alpha = 0.5,
    color = NA) + #getting rid of black outlines
  labs(
    x = "Flipper Length (mm)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Species") +
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

mass <- penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x=(body_mass_g)/1000, fill=species))+
  geom_density(
    aes(y = after_stat(count)),
    alpha = 0.85,
    color = NA) + #getting rid of black outlines
  labs(
    x = "Body Mass (kg)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Species") +
  theme_bw()

(depth / length / flipper / mass) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")+
  plot_annotation(title = "Penguin Body Measurements Across Species:")
```
Now, I'm creating a summary table with averages of each body measurement for each of the `r n_distinct(penguins$species)` species in this penguin dataset, and including sample size (n) to see the distribution of sampling effort.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-penguins
#| tbl-cap: "Average penguin bill length, bill depth, flipper length, and body mass by species. Sample size (n) displayed for each species."
penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    "Bill Length (mm)" = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    "Bill Depth (mm)" = mean(bill_depth_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    "Flipper Length (mm)" = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    "Body Mass (kg)" = (mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)/1000),
    "n" = n())|>
  rename(Species = species) |> #making species variable name capitalized for table
  kbl(digits=2, # make it a kable table, rounding to 2 digits
      caption = "Average Body Measurements for Palmer Penguins") |> 
  kable_classic() |> # add a theme, kable classic
  column_spec(5, bold = TRUE, background = "turquoise") 
  
```

#### Takeaways:

As shown in @fig-penguinplot, body measurements (bill depth, bill length, flipper length, and body mass) vary across species. Mean values across species (with sample size) are summarized in @tbl-penguins.  

Gentoo penguins have a greater body mass on average when compared to Adelie and Chinstrap species (@tbl-penguins), which as illustrated by @fig-penguinplot, may be linked to their larger flipper length.
